limitations_and_boundaries: The study uses cancer cell lines and pharmacological compounds; findings may not generalize to normal tissues or in vivo contexts.
The atlas is based on in vitro perturbations; in vivo validation is lacking.
The Mosaic platform's 'cell village' approach may introduce specific batch effects despite optimization.
Gene set enrichment analyses rely on predefined signatures (e.g., MSigDB.c6) which may not capture all relevant biology.
Statistical tests (Welch's t-test) were used without correction for multiple comparisons in some analyses.
The study focuses on transcriptional responses; post-transcriptional and proteomic effects are not captured.
Cell cycle phase analysis is based on odds ratios from aggregated data; single-cell resolution of phase assignments may have technical noise.
The atlas includes only 50 cell lines, which may not represent the full diversity of cancer genotypes.
Drug concentrations used (0.05, 0.5, 5.0 uM) may not reflect clinically relevant doses.
The preprint status indicates the study has not yet been peer-reviewed.

experiments_or_tasks: Comparison of log2 odds ratios of cells in G2/M phase for HDAC inhibitors (Belinostat, Panobinostat, Carbamazepine, Tucidinostat) and microtubule inhibitors.

Computation of odds ratios for the percentage of cells in each cell cycle phase relative to control for CDK inhibitors Palbociclib, Dinaciclib, Abemaciclib, AT5719, and Ribociclib across 47 cellular models and 3 drug concentrations.

Differential gene set expression analysis using Vision scores for a RAS/RAF pathway signature across cell lines stratified by KRAS, BRAF-V600E, and RAS/RAF wild-type genotypes, treated with Dabrafenib or RMC-6236 at multiple doses.

Generation of a giga-scale single-cell perturbation atlas (Tahoe-100M) comprising 100 million transcriptomic profiles from 50 cancer cell lines treated with 1,100 small-molecule perturbations using the Mosaic platform.
